items.front: In the shared responsibility model, security of the cloud or security in the cloud: which one is the customer's job?
items.extra: [While AWS manages security of the cloud, you are responsible for security in the cloud](../facts/well-architected.md#well-architected-security-in-the-cloud-you-retain-control).

items.front: In AWS, does AWS copy your resources to another Region for you?
items.back: No. You turn on a replication or copy feature yourself.
items.extra: A resource exists only in its own Region [unless you explicitly use a replication or copy feature offered by an AWS service or replicate the resource yourself](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-no-automatic-cross-region-replication).

items.front: In AWS, a synchronous standby in a second Availability Zone or an asynchronous replica in a second Region: which one can lose the latest writes in a failover?
items.back: The asynchronous replica in the second Region.
items.extra: With an [asynchronously replicated datastore](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-async-cross-region-replication-may-lose-data) across Regions, there is [the possibility of data loss or inconsistency when you fail over](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-async-cross-region-replication-may-lose-data).

items.front: In AWS, users in one city far from any Region need single-digit millisecond latency to your EC2 instances. LOWEST latency?
items.back: Run the instances in a Local Zone near that city.
items.extra: Local Zones are built for workloads that need [single-digit millisecond latency](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-faq-local-zones-single-digit-millisecond-latency-workloads).

items.front: In AWS, static images in one Amazon S3 bucket load slowly for users around the world. LEAST operational overhead?
items.back: Amazon CloudFront, which serves the images from edge locations.
items.extra: [Amazon CloudFront, Amazon Route 53, AWS Firewall Manager, AWS Shield, and AWS WAF services are provided through AWS Edge Locations](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-edge-location-services).

items.front: In AWS, AZ name or AZ ID: which one names the same physical Availability Zone in every account?
items.back: The AZ ID, for example use1-az2.
items.extra: An AZ ID names [the same physical location in every AWS account](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-az-id-same-physical-location-every-account).

items.front: In the shared responsibility model, Amazon EC2 or Amazon S3: on which one does the customer patch the operating system?
items.extra: On EC2 the customer owns the [guest operating system (including updates and security patches)](../facts/well-architected.md#well-architected-customer-responsible-for-guest-os-apps-security-groups); on S3 [AWS operates the infrastructure layer, the operating system, and platforms](../facts/well-architected.md#well-architected-abstracted-services-aws-runs-os-customer-manages-data).

items.front: In AWS, a team wants to review one workload for security, cost and high availability against AWS best practices, with no additional charge for the tool. Which tool?
items.extra: The tool lets you [review your workloads against current AWS best practices](../facts/well-architected.md#well-architected-faq-tool-reviews-workloads-against-best-practices), with [no additional charge](../facts/well-architected.md#well-architected-faq-tool-no-additional-charge).

items.front: In AWS, every Region has {{c1::at least three}} Availability Zones.
The Well-Architected reliability pillar says to run every production workload in {{c1::at least two Availability Zones (AZs) in a Region}}.
In AWS, the Availability Zones of one Region are all {{c1::within 100 km}} of each other.
In AWS, network latency between the Availability Zones of one Region is {{c1::single-digit millisecond}}.
